$comment: Single source of truth for the combined Filecheck × Print Options demos. shop.html?product=<slug> reads its chrome and blueprint URL from here; the landing page builds its category cards from the same entries. Blueprints live in /configs/po/ (11 of them emitted by tools/make-po-configs.mjs, the two pilots hand-authored) and every one is price-verified by product-options' check.mjs against samples/manifest.json.

business-cards.title: Business cards
business-cards.copy: The everyday baseline: quantity breaks and finish uplifts priced by Print Options, while Filecheck checks size, bleed, safe zone and fonts; the artwork is checked, never priced from.
business-cards.shows: Shows: cart gating, quantity tiers, finish uplifts, double-sided page count
tryIt: Upload the good card, it passes clean.
Try the no-bleed version: the warning explains exactly what will get trimmed wrong.
Switch to double-sided; the same one-page file is suddenly missing its back.
Stack finishes and watch the order the uplifts apply in.
business-cards.blurb: Quantity breaks and finish uplifts priced live; size, bleed, safe zone and fonts checked.

flyers.title: Flyers
flyers.copy: Pick a size and sides; the price and the artwork check both follow your choices. This page's options are rendered by Print Options; the upload is inspected by Filecheck against exactly what you selected.
flyers.shows: Shows: selections drive the check, quantity tiers, double-sided page count
tryIt: Download the A5 sample below and upload it, it passes.
Click A4. The check re-runs against the new size; same file, now wrong, nothing re-uploaded.
Switch to double-sided: a one-page file is suddenly incomplete.
Watch the price follow every change you make.
flyers.blurb: Size and sides drive both the price and the artwork check.

folded-leaflet.title: Folded leaflet
folded-leaflet.copy: Folding is where customer files most often go wrong. Two landscape spreads, always; and the fold you pick sets how much clearance your text needs from the creases.
folded-leaflet.shows: Shows: fold sets the safe zone, exact page count, orientation
tryIt: Upload the two-page tri-fold sample, it passes.
Try the one-page file: a leaflet needs both sides, and the finding says so.
Switch from half fold to tri fold and see the safe zone tighten.
folded-leaflet.blurb: The fold sets how much clearance your text needs from the creases.

stickers.title: Die-cut stickers
stickers.copy: No size inputs anywhere; the sticker is priced from your artwork's own trim size. Upload something bigger and the price follows. Transparent backgrounds cut best, and we warn when yours isn't.
stickers.shows: Shows: priced from the file, transparency check, area tiers
tryIt: Upload the transparent logo; the detected size drives the price.
Try the white-background version: same art, but the warning explains what the cutter will see.
Bump the quantity past 100 and watch the per-sticker rate drop.
stickers.blurb: No size inputs; priced from your artwork's own trim size.

thesis.title: Thesis printing & binding
thesis.copy: No page-count dropdowns to fill in. Upload your document and the price is built from what Filecheck finds inside it; total pages, and which of them actually use colour.
thesis.shows: Shows: priced from the file, colour/mono split, locked PDFs rejected
tryIt: Upload the 48-page sample; the price breaks down into 12 colour pages and 36 mono pages, each at its own rate.
Switch to black & white throughout; same file, one flat per-page rate.
Try the locked PDF: rejected before it can ever jam a print queue.
thesis.blurb: The price is built from what Filecheck finds inside your document.

booklet.title: Saddle-stitched booklet
booklet.copy: You pick the pagination; the file must honour it; the inner-stock price is computed from the pages actually found in your upload. A wizard walks the whole order through step by step.
booklet.shows: Shows: wizard layout, page count enforced, per-page stock pricing
tryIt: Pick 16 pages and upload the 16-page sample; it passes and prices per page.
Try the 13-page file: saddle stitch needs a multiple of four, and the check enforces the count you picked.
Switch A5 to A4; the same file is re-judged against the new size.
booklet.blurb: You pick the pagination; the file must honour it. A wizard walks the order.

banner.title: PVC banner
banner.copy: Type the finished size, pick a finish; the area price and the artwork check both follow. Hem and eyelets need 25 mm of bleed; trimmed needs 3. The check always knows which one you asked for.
banner.shows: Shows: typed size drives the check, finish sets bleed, area tiers
tryIt: Upload the 3 × 1 m sample at the default size, it passes.
Change the width; the same file is re-checked against the new size, nothing re-uploaded.
Switch finishing from hem-and-eyelets to trimmed and watch the bleed requirement drop from 25 mm to 3.
banner.blurb: Type the finished size, pick a finish; area price and check both follow.

banner-auto.title: Banner, priced from your artwork
banner-auto.copy: The inverse of the classic banner page: no size inputs at all. The upload is the specification. Filecheck measures the trim size and Print Options prices the square metres it reports.
banner-auto.shows: Shows: the upload sets the price, area tier breaks, DPI at real size
tryIt: Upload the 3 × 1 m banner, 4.5 m² priced at the small-run rate.
Now the 4.5 × 1.8 m one: 8.1 m² crosses the tier break and the rate per square metre drops.
There is nothing else to fill in. That is the point.
banner-auto.blurb: No size inputs at all; the upload is the specification.

poster.title: Custom size poster
poster.copy: The two products staying in their lanes: the price comes from the size you type, never from the file; while Filecheck judges whether your artwork is actually sharp enough at that size.
poster.shows: Shows: DPI is relative to print size, dimensions pricing, price floor
tryIt: Upload the low-res image at the default 50 × 70 cm, borderline.
Grow the poster to 100 × 150 cm: same file, now clearly not sharp enough. Resolution is relative.
Upload the A1 sample and shrink the size, suddenly everything passes.
poster.blurb: Price from the size you type; sharpness judged against it.

rollup.title: Roll-up banner stand
rollup.copy: A fixed-size product with hardware; and a trap: the visible area is 850 × 2000 mm, but the file must be 850 × 2150 because the bottom 150 mm disappears into the cassette.
rollup.shows: Shows: fixed template, the cassette tail, hardware add-ons
tryIt: Upload the correct file (with the tail), it passes.
Now the classic mistake: artwork sized to the visible 2000 mm. Rejected, with a finding that explains the tail.
Nothing on this page changes the check; not every product needs the bridge.
rollup.blurb: Visible 850 × 2000 mm, file 850 × 2150; the tail hides in the cassette.

tshirt.title: Printed t-shirt
tshirt.copy: Raster-first checking: a flat white background will print as a white box on the shirt, and we warn before it does. Resolution is judged at the chest-print size you pick, and dark garments add an underbase.
tshirt.shows: Shows: background warning, DPI at print size, garment options
tryIt: Upload the white-background logo; the warning explains what will actually print.
Swap in the transparent version: same art, clean pass.
Switch A4 chest to A3 full front; the resolution target follows the print size.
tshirt.blurb: A flat white background prints as a white box; we warn before it does.

mug.title: Wrap-print mug
mug.copy: Template products: the artwork must fit a physical wrap. Picking the bigger mug changes the template the same file is checked against; and the handle keep-out never moves.
mug.shows: Shows: template follows the mug, aspect ratio, handle keep-out
tryIt: Upload the 11 oz wrap; it matches the template exactly.
Switch to the 15 oz mug: template mismatch appears instantly, no re-upload.
Try the square image; a 40:17 wrap and a 1:1 file were never going to agree.
mug.blurb: The artwork must fit a physical wrap; the handle keep-out never moves.

canvas.title: Photo canvas
canvas.copy: A consumer photo product with a hidden physical requirement: gallery wrap folds the photo around the frame, which needs 38 mm of extra image on every side. Mirror wrap needs none. The check knows which you picked.
canvas.shows: Shows: wrap sets the bleed, DPI vs frame size, forgiving thresholds
tryIt: Upload the portrait photo on the 30 × 40 frame, passes, canvas is forgiving.
Pick 60 × 90 with gallery wrap: two findings, in plain language; resolution and missing wrap allowance.
Switch to mirror wrap and the bleed requirement disappears.

samples.label: Panorama, wrong shape for a portrait frame

canvas.blurb: Gallery wrap folds 38 mm around every side; mirror wrap needs none.
